body.statement:
Let \(D_{n,r}\) be a square-integrable martingale-difference triangular array adapted to \(\mathcal F_{n,r}\), let \(\sigma_n>0\), and put \(Q_n=\sum_r\mathbb E[D_{n,r}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,r-1}]\).  If \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\) and, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sigma_n^{-2}\sum_r\mathbb E\!\left[D_{n,r}^2
 \mathbf 1\{|D_{n,r}|>\varepsilon\sigma_n\}\mid\mathcal F_{n,r-1}\right]
 \xrightarrow{p}0,
\]
then \(\sigma_n^{-1}\sum_rD_{n,r}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\).

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem. Let {ξ_nj} be a martingale-difference array. If, as n → ∞, (i) Σ_j v_nj → σ² in probability, with σ² a positive constant; (ii) for every ε > 0, the sum Σ_j P(ξ_nj² 1{|ξ_nj| > ε} | E_{n,j−1}) converges in probability to zero (a Lindeberg condition); then ξ_n1 + ··· + ξ_nn converges in distribution to N(0, σ²).

upstream.citation: B. M. Brown (1971), Martingale Central Limit Theorems, Annals of Mathematical Statistics 42(1), 59–66

attestation.note: Direct transcription from Pollard's author-hosted scan, Theorem VIII.1 on printed p. 171; mathematical glyphs and convergence wording normalized for plain text. Here Pollard's P(·|E) denotes conditional expectation, and scaling ξ_nj=D_nj/σ_n gives the run's lemma.
